report.summary: verify_ledger implementation missing from slice, so tamper proof cannot be audited. _ends_without_newline opens file while another process may hold write handle, risking sharing violation on Windows. No inter-process append serialisation, writes can interleave. Secret floor re-scan handles provenance correctly.
risks: verify_ledger function body absent from provided context; full tamper-evidence guarantee unconfirmed.

Windows sharing violation in _ends_without_newline: opens ledger for reading while another process may have it open for append, causing PermissionError and crashing append instead of gracefully handling torn line.
No cross-process append serialisation: two daemons/processes appending simultaneously can interleave writes, silently corrupting the chain (though hash chain will break, detection is reactive).
_normalize_entry silently drops unexpected keys inside 'trust' dict, which contradicts the strict-reject posture for other sub-dicts; could hide mis-specified callers.
todos: Implement verify_ledger body or provide it for audit.
Consider file-level lock (e.g., portalocker) on Windows for cross-process append safety.
Change _ends_without_newline to read last byte without re-opening, or use append-mode with atomic read/write using os.lseek?
Validate trust sub-fields to reject unknown keys.

handoff.suggestion: Ensure verify_ledger is actually written; the missing body is the top risk. For cross-process safety, use a multi-process aware locking mechanism on Windows (e.g., msvcrt.locking or portalocker) around appends to prevent interleaving and file sharing conflicts.
